Article 9 states that a person who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country ceases to be a citizen of India.
India does not allow dual citizenship.
India does not allow dual citizenship.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 9 mandates that voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship results in automatic loss of Indian citizenship.
Dual citizenship is strictly prohibited under Indian law as per Article 9.
Article 10 guarantees the continuance of citizenship rights to any citizen, subject to laws enacted by Parliament.
Article 11 authorizes Parliament to make provisions for the acquisition, termination, and all other citizenship matters.
The Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted by Parliament using its constitutional authority under Article 11.

rows: Cessation of Indian citizenship upon voluntarily acquiring citizenship of another country.
Guarantees that a citizen continues to be a citizen, subject to Parliamentary legislation.
Empowers Parliament to regulate acquisition, termination, and other citizenship matters.

blocks.content: Article 10 ensures that every person who is or is deemed to be a citizen of India shall continue to be a citizen, subject to laws made by Parliament.

items: Article 9 is frequently cited in exams regarding the prohibition of dual citizenship in India.
Parliament's exclusive right to legislate on citizenship acquisition and termination is derived from Article 11.
The Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted directly on the basis of Article 11.

blocks.content:
Article 11 gives Parliament the authority to make laws related to:
• Acquisition of citizenship
• Termination of citizenship
• Other matters related to citizenship

Based on this article, Parliament enacted the Citizenship Act, 1955.
